full_judgment:
Ms. Nazmun Ara Sultana, J:- By this writ Petition the petitioner sheikh Shahidul Islam has impugned the order no. 3 dated 21.9.2005 passed by the learned judge of Artha Rin Adalat second court Bagerhat in Artha Jari Case no. 78 of 2005 rejecting the application of the petitioner under section 49 read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 2003 praying for allowing him to clear up the outstanding dues of the decree holder bank in 4 installments within one year time. 

 3. This present petitioner appeared, in that Artha Rin suit and filed written statement and ultimately that suit was decreed on compromise on 27.11.2004. As per that Compromise decree the writ petitioner was to pay the entire claim of the plaintiff hank Which was Tk. 3.48,835/- in 4 installments within one year time. But the petitioner failed to pay that decreetal amount and consequently the above mentioned execution case was started on 6.8.2005. On 21.9.2005 this petitioner appeared in that execution ease- and filed an application under section 49 read with section 57 of the Artha: Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for allowing him to pay the decreetal amount to the plaintiff bank in 4 installments within one year time. The learned Judge of the Execution Court; after hearing both the parties and considering the facts and circumstances rejected the said prayer of this petitioner by the impugned order. 

 5. The respondent no.2 Agrani bank- the plaintiff decree, holder has contested this rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition. 

 6. We have heard the learned advocates of both the sides and examined the relevant papers including the impugned order-the annexure A and the compromise decree- the annexure-C. 

 7. It appears from the annexure-C that this petitioner came to a settlement with the plaintiff bank admitting the claim of the plaintiff-bank and also agreeing to pay the entire outstanding' amount, i.e. Tk. 3,48,835/- in 4 installments within a period of one year. Admittedly this petitioner failed' to comply with that compromise decree and consequently the plaintiff-bank instituted the execution case. Thereafter on 21.9.2005 this District Judge & Ors (Nazatun Ara  Sultana) 327  writ petitioner appeared in the execution case and prayed for allowing him to pay the decreetal amount in 4 installments within one year time. But the learned Judge of Execution Court rejected the said prayer making observation that this petitioner already failed to pay back the decreetal amount in 4 installments within one year time as per terms of the compromise decree. 

 8. Mr. Afsana Begun appearing on behalf of Mr. S.N. Goswami the-learned advocate for the petitioner has submitted that this writ petitioner due to acute financial constraint could not pay the decreetal amount in time, but he is very much eager to pay hack the outstanding dues of ;the plaintiff bank and that considering the financial crisis of the petitioner he, on humanitarian ground, may be given another chance to pay the decreetal  amount in 4 installments  within one year time. 

 9. The learned advocate Mr. Md. Mozibur Rahman has appearing for the respondent no.2 has consented in giving another reasonable opportunity to this petitioner to pay the decreetal amount. 

 10.  Considering the submissions of the learned advocates of the both the sides and also the facts and circumstances we are inclined to give another chance to the petitioner to pay the decreetal amount in installments. Accordingly, it is ordered that the rule be made absolute on contest without.-any order a cost. 

 11. The writ petitioner is permitted to pay the decreetal amount in 4 equal installments to the respondent no.2 within a period of 8 (eight) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment by the execution court. If the petitioner fails to -pay any of the installments the execution case328 (Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J) Abdul Aziz Ors Vs. will proceed in accordance with law. The petitioner will deposit the amount of installments in the execution court. The order of stay grunted at the time of issuance of the rule stands vacated.
